geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the fractional book clip with a more direct clipping operator to simplify the dominant mass and reduce the over-sculpted wedge reading.
Keep the more coherent major portion of the mass as the primary bar datum.
Add a true courtyard/public void to repair the missing active ground threshold and align the building with neighborhood-living semantics.
Use a moderate margin to carve a usable public space rather than a decorative subtraction.
Open the courtyard toward the verified access edge so the street threshold becomes legible.
Make the new courtyard-wrapped composition the root so the public void governs the rebuilt massing hierarchy.

graph_edits.rationale: The current dominant mass reads as a single tapered wedge with weak neighborhood-building hierarchy; split it into a clearer bar/support relationship to recover readable program organization.
Keep the primary datum as a long bar aligned to the site logic rather than a squat sculptural object.
Strengthen the public void so it clearly opens to the verified access side and becomes a legible ground threshold.
Widen the carve to produce a meaningful entry court rather than a decorative notch.
Increase the carve depth so the ground response becomes spatially legible in all views.

rationale: The four views read as one compact but overly faceted tapered mass rather than a clear neighborhood-living building. The silhouette is coherent in each view, but the form does not resolve into a strong dominant bar, support hierarchy, or legible ground/public void. The green parcel is roughly occupied, but the mass appears to just sit within it rather than organizing the parcel into an expressive open-space figure. The blue frontage edge is not convincingly answered by a public threshold; the mass remains sealed and semantically neutral/opposite to the access edge. The object also reads more like a sculpted stepped/pyramidal volume than a capacity-aware mixed-use bar with active base and clear public cut, so program fit fails. References suggest either a courtyard/interlocking-wing strategy or a calmer bar with a distinct entry carve, but this candidate currently lacks both.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much more coherent as a courtyard/campus composition than this candidate; do not imitate its fragmentation without preserving a clear public threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Use a dominant courtyard/void with interlocking wings and stepped upper masses while keeping the ground plane legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This candidate is far more sculptural and vertical; the reference is a calm pavilion, not a stepped object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low-rise bar can gain program legibility through a clear entry setback/canopy and a strong horizontal ground response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a streetwall/midrise composition; candidate does not show a comparable active base or coherent urban edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Attached volumes and staggered massing can support a neighborhood program when hierarchy remains readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual only; this candidate does not achieve the open, inhabitable sectional logic shown here and risks reading as an isolated sculptural wedge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced section can create inhabitable roof/void relationships and a strong public edge.
